This claim petition emanates in respect of the injuries sustained by the Petitioner by name Sujatha (herein after referred to as the petitioner) in respect of the Road Traffic Accident dated 22.01.2023.

2. Succinctly stated the facts germane to the lis involved in this petition are briefly summarized as follows:
That on 22.01.2023 at about 3.00 p.m., when the petitioner was proceeding as a pedestrian with observing all SCCH 15 3 MVC No.1529/2023 traffic rules and when she reached Mysore main road, in front of RV College, Kengeri, Bengaluru, at that time, respondent's motorcycle bearing Reg.No.KA-05-LH-1066 (herein after referred to as the offending vehicle) came in a rash and negligent manner with high speed and dashed against the Petitioner, resulting in the accident.
It is submitted that the Petitioner sustained grievous injuries all over the body due to the impact of the accident.
3. Immediately, after the accident petitioner was shifted to R.R hospital and then she was shifted to Sanjay Gandhi hospital, wherein she took treatment as an inpatient.
Hence, the petitioner has claimed compensation of Rs.15,00,000/- with cost and interest at the rate of 12% p.a in the interest of justice and equity.
4. In pursuance of service of notice issued to the Respondents, Respondent No.1 remained absent and he was placed exparte.

SCCH 15 4 MVC No.1529/2023 Respondent No.2 filed Written Statement contending as follows:
The respondent No.2 admitted that it has issued policy to the offending vehicle in favour of the respondent No.1.
The Respondent No.2 in its Objection Statement denied the accident was caused by rash and negligent riding of the rider of the offending vehicle.
The rider of the offending vehicle did not have valid and effective riding license.
The age, avocation of the petitioner is denied.
The petition is bad for non joinder of necessary parties.
Hence, on these grounds Respondent No.2 has prayed to dismiss the petition against it.

5. Vide order dated 20.10.2023 the following issues were framed by this Tribunal :-
ISSUES Sujatha.S vs Rajashekar on 6 August, 2025 Indian Kanoon - http://indiankanoon.org/doc/108403429/
2 1) Whether the Petitioner proves that she had sustained grievous injuries in the Road Traffic Accident that occurred on 22.01.2023 at about 3.00 p.m., near Mysore main road, in front of RV College, Mysore Road, Kengeri, Bengaluru, due to the rash SCCH 15 5 MVC No.1529/2023 and negligent riding of the Motorcycle bearing Reg.No.KA-05-LH-1066 by its rider?
2) Whether the Petitioner is entitled for the compensation as prayed for?

entities.text: ISSUES Sujatha.S vs Rajashekar on 6 August, 2025 Indian Kanoon
entities.label: PRECEDENT

sentences.text:
If yes, what is the quantum and who is liable to pay?
3) What Order or Award?

6. In order to prove the case of the Petitioner, the Petitioner got examined herself as PW.1 and examined two witnesses as PW.2 and 3 and relied upon Ex.P.1 to 22 and the Respondent No.2 has examined one witness as RW.1 and relied upon Ex.R1.
7.
Oral submissions were advanced by Ld. Counsel for parties in this case.

Having perused the records my issue wise findings run as under:-
 Issue No.1 : In the Affirmative.
 Issue No.2 : Partly in the Affirmative.

Issue No.3 : As per the Final Order  for the following :
 SCCH 15 6 MVC No.1529/2023  REASONS 8.
Issue No.1:
Before adjudication of the issue with respect to the compensation it is quintessential to adjudicate on the issue of negligence.

It is the asseveration of the petitioner that the accident took place due to the rash and negligent riding of the rider of the motorcycle bearing Reg.No.KA-05-LH-1066 (herein after referred to as offending vehicle).

9. On the aspect of the manner of the accident the petitioner got examined himself as PW.1 and in her chief- examination she has deposed that on 22.01.2023 at about 3.00 p.m. when she was proceeding as a pedestrian from BIMS towards RV College gate, Mysore main road, Kengeri, at that time the rider of the offending vehicle came in a rash and negligent manner and dashed against the petitioner, resulting in grievous injuries to the petitioner.

In order to substantiate the same the petitioner has produced Ex.P1 - FIR which discloses that the case has been registered against the rider of the offending vehicle and it is also mentioned that the rider of the offending vehicle dashed from the side without stopping the vehicle.
Ex.P2 is the Sujatha.
S vs Rajashekar

on 6 August, 2025 Indian Kanoon - http://indiankanoon.org/doc/108403429/
3 Complaint which discloses that the complaint has been lodged on 24.01.2023 and spot sketch discloses that the accident has taken place on the middle of the road and the petitioner was coming from the passage between the divider probably in order to cross the road when the accident occured.

Ex.P5 is the IMV report which discloses that the front left side of the motorcycle had sustained damages and after completion of investigation the charge sheet has been filed against the rider of the motorcycle for the offences under sec.279 and 338 of IPC.
Ex.P8 is the Order sheet in CC No.3217/2023 which discloses that the rider of the offending vehicle has pleaded guilty and paid the fine amount.
The hospital records also discloses that the petitioner was brought to the hospital on 22.01.2023 SCCH 15 8 MVC No.1529/2023 under the history of RTA.
These documents show that the accident has occurred due to the negligence of the rider of the offending vehicle.

11. PW.1 is cross-examined by the learned counsel for the respondent No.2 and in the cross-examination of PW.1 she admitted that the accident has taken place in the front road of RV college and there is heavy traffic on the said road, there is no signal and denied that the accident has taken place in the middle of the road.
It is the contention of the respondent that without observing oncoming vehicles, the petitioner abruptly crossed the road and hence the accident has taken place due to her negligence.

The learned counsel for the respondent No.2 has also relied on the decision ILR 2004 KAR 1104, between Koosappa Poojari Vs. K. Sadabba and others, wherein Hon'ble Apex Court has pleased to observed that:
"Motor vehicles Act 1988 (59/88 - Sec.173 (1) contributory negligence - claimant had crossed the road where he has not supposed to cross - held - certain degree of contributory negligence will have to be attributed to him - if a SCCH 15 9 MVC No.1529/2023 pedestrian is crossing over a roadway at any place other than which is meant for pedestrian crossing he can not claim any specific precedence and the responsibility for causing the accident - pedestrian has to share the negligence along with the driver."

entities.text: Koosappa Poojari Vs. K. Sadabba and others
entities.label: PRECEDENT

sentences.text: 12. Even though the counsel for respondent relied on the said decision however, the accident has taken place somewhere in the middle of the road and hence rider of the offending vehicle also ought to have noticed the petitioner on the road and could have slowed down his bike or applied brake or taken suitable caution to avoid the accident.

It does not appear to be a case that the petitioner all of a sudden crossed the road and hence it is due to the fact that the rider of the offending vehicle was riding at high speed that he could not control the speed of his vehicle and could not avoid the accident.

Except the suggestion that the accident has taken place due to the negligence on the petitioner side nothing much is elicited in the cross-examination of PW.1 to prove that the accident took place due to the negligence or rashness on the part of the petitioner.
The petitioner clearly and SCCH 15 10 MVC No.1529/2023 categorically deposed about the manner of the accident.
Though she admits in her cross-examination that she was crossing the road however it is not the case that she suddenly ran on the road or entered the road.
No such evidence is placed on record and on the other hand the accident has taken place on the middle of the road and not while just trying to enter the road.
In addition after investigation the charge sheet is filed against the rider of the offending vehicle alone.
If it was a case of contributory negligent then both would have been arraigned as Sujatha.

Indian Kanoon - http://indiankanoon.org/doc/108403429/
4 accused in the charge sheet.
The oral testimony of PW.1 has stood unrebutted.
There is no material on record which suggests falsity or untruth in the oral testimony of PW.1 as to the facts and circumstances surrounding cause of the accident.
PW.1 has also denied the suggestion imputing the cause of the accident to be due to her negligence.
The fact that the rider of the offending vehicle has already been charge sheeted for the offences under Sec.279 and 338 of IPC itself is strong circumstance to support the oral testimony of PW.1.
SCCH 15 11 MVC No.1529/2023 The certified copies of FIR, charge sheet, IMV report and Spot mahazar also corroborate the oral testimony of PW.1.
In view of medical records there is no dispute regarding the nature of injuries sustained by PW.1 in the above accident.
In view of the said discussion it is satisfactorily established that PW.1 suffered grievous injuries on account of rash and negligent riding by the offending vehicle at the relevant time.

Hence, issue No.1 is answered in favour of the petitioner and in the 'Affirmative'.
13. Issue No.2
: In view of the findings on issue No.1 in favour of petitioner, the petitioner is entitled for compensation.
The computation of compensation will have to be decided separately under various heads.
14. MEDICAL OR TREATMENT EXPENSES:

The petitioner has produced Ex.P9 - Wound certificate of Sanjay Gandhi Institute of Trauma & Orthopaedics which discloses that the petitioner had sustained grievous injuries and she has swelling, tenderness and deformity in right knee and right SCCH 15 12 MVC No.1529/2023 proximal tibia fracture along with other complications and she has taken treatment from 22.01.2023 to 01.02.2023.

entities.text: Sanjay Gandhi Institute of Trauma & Orthopaedics
entities.label: ORG

sentences.text: As far as medical bills are concerned the petitioner has produced Ex.P11 & 20 medical bills to the tune of Rs.75,066/-.
Hence petitioner is entitled to an amount of Rs.75,066/- under this head.
15. PAIN AND SUFFERING:
As per the medical documents the petitioner has suffered grievous injuries and Ex.P9 discloses that the petitioner has sustained swelling, tenderness and deformity and right proximal tibia fracture.
It is not possible to ascertain quantum compensation admissible to petitioner for the shock, pain and sufferings etc., which he actually suffered due to the accidental injuries.

Keeping in view the trauma and nature of the injuries suffered by the petitioner and duration of the treatment taken by him etc., an amount of Rs.30,000/- is awarded to him towards pain and sufferings.
Thus, he is an awarded an amount of Rs.30,000/- under this head.
SCCH 15 13 MVC No.1529/2023 16. LOSS OF ACTUAL EARNINGS:
In his evidence PW.1 has submitted she was aged about 50 years and she was working as coolie and earning Rs.25,000/- p.m.

In the absence of any material as to the monthly earnings of the Petitioner it would be proper to assume the monthly earnings of the petitioner as per the notional income as on the date of the accident, as per the guidelines of Lok-Adalat chart.

As per the relevant period the notional income is taken as Rs.16,000/- p.m.
Taking into consideration that the petitioner due to the injuries might not have been in a position to work for at least 3 months.

Hence, as such the petitioner is entitled to an amount of Rs.16,000 X 3 =
48,000/- under this head.

5 17.
LOSS OF FUTURE EARNINGS DUE TO DISABILITY:
The petitioner has claimed in her affidavit she was permanent disability to her right leg.
As per the evidence of PW.2 her impairment is not progressive and will not improve in future and hence it is submitted by the petitioner that she cannot pursue her work as before the accident.

In support of the same, PW.3 - Orthopedic Surgeon has deposed regarding the disability assessed by him and he has stated that the petitioner had sustained permanent physical disability 40% of right lower limb which is 13% to the whole body.
The above mentioned disability is issued in terms of Central Government Notification.

PW.2 is subjected to cross- examined by the learned counsel for the respondent No.2 wherein he has deposed that he is not treated the petitioner nor given any further treatment and only assessed her disability on 26.08.2024 after almost 1 year after discharge of the petitioner and as per the X-ray to fracture is united.
PW.3 has denied that the chances for further recovery.
She has deposed that the implants are not removed and denied that if the implants have removed then the disability can reduce.
PW.3 has also denied that he has assessed the disability on the higher side.
As per the evidence of PW.3 which discloses that he has stated that 28% loss of mobility and almost 18% loss of stability component.
Though the SCCH 15 15 MVC No.1529/2023 disability stated on the higher side.
The disability assessed by the PW.3 is supported by the evaluation and proforma of assessment.
Hence there is nothing to disbelieve the disability assessed by PW.3.
since it is as per the government notification as per 2018.
Accordingly, above mentioned disability can be read in evidence in terms of the observations made by the Hon'ble High Court of Karnataka in Bajaj Allianz Insurance Company Limited Vs Union of India.

entities.text: Bajaj Allianz Insurance Company Limited Vs Union of India
entities.label: PRECEDENT

sentences.text: PW.3 has admitted that he has assessed physical disability not functional disability.
The petitioner is working as labour and she can continue even in future and she would have some difficulties in agricultural work.
The evidence of PW.3 discloses that the petitioner had sustained physical disability at 40% to right lower limb which is 13% to the whole body.
The monthly income of the petitioner is already assessed at Rs.16,000/- at the relevant time.

As far as,
age of the petitioner at the time of the accident is concerned on perusal of the petitioner's Aadhaar card Ex.P13 the date of birth of the petitioner is SCCH 15 16 MVC No.1529/2023 21.10.1971.
Going by the same, the age of petitioner as on date of accident i.e., 22.01.2023 was around 52 years.

Therefore, in view of the dictum laid down by the Hon'ble Supreme Court in Sarla Verma and others Vs. Delhi Corporation and another (2009) 6 SCC 121, which has also been upheld by the Constitution Bench of the Hon'ble Supreme Court in the recent judgment dated 31.10.2017 given in the case of National Insurance Company Ltd. vs. Pranay Sethi & Ors.

entities.label: PRECEDENT

entities.label: PRECEDENT

sentences.text:
SLP (Civil) No. 25590 of 2014,
the multiplier of '11' is held applicable for calculating the loss of future earnings of petitioner arising out of her above disability.

The loss of future earnings of petitioner due to her above injury and permanent physical disability comes to Rs.2,74,560/- (Rs.16,000/- X 12 X 11 X 13%) and the same is awarded to him as compensation under this head.

sentences.text: Loss of Amenities:

In view of the nature of injuries sustained by the petitioner, the extent of permanent physical SCCH 15 17 MVC No.1529/2023 disability and the extended period of medical treatment, the petitioner is granted a sum of Rs.20,000/- under this head.
20. Attendant's charges, Special diet and Conveyance:
The facts show that physical condition of the petitioner is such that he might have to taken the help of an attendant.
Further, he would be requiring conveyance for movement.
His avocation has been hit due to her disablement.
He might have spent considerable amount towards special diet during her treatment.
Therefore, petitioner is granted Rs.20,000/- under this head.

21. TOTAL COMPENSATION TO WHICH THE PETITIONER IS ENTITLED:
To sum up, the Petitioner is entitled for compensation under the following heads :
1. Pain, shock & Suffering  30,000/-
2. Loss of amenities  20,000/-
3. Loss of income during the laid  48,000/-
up period SCCH 15 18 MVC No.1529/2023 4.

Attendant's charges, Extra diet,  20,000/-
and conveyance 5.

Medical expenses  75,066/-
6. Loss of Future Income 2,74,560/-
Total 4,67,626/-
Thus, totally the Petitioner is awarded compensation of 4,67,626/- with costs and simple interest at 6% p.a. from the date of this petition till the date of realization.

22. Regarding Liability: This Court has arrived at the conclusion that the accident has been occurred by the rash and negligent riding on the part of the rider of the offending motorcycle bearing Reg.No.KA-05-LH-1066.

As far as the liability is concerned the Assistant Manager of respondent No.2 insurance company is examined as RW.1 and he has deposed that the offending vehicle was insured with own damage coverage as well as 3 rd party liability.

RW.1 in his cross-examination has admitted that the policy Sujatha.S vs Rajashekar on 6 August, 2025 Indian Kanoon - http://indiankanoon.org/doc/108403429/
7 was valid as on the date of the accident and admitted that there is SCCH 15 19 MVC No.1529/2023 no signal that the pedestrian cannot cross the road at the said spot.
On the other hand the fact that there was opening on the road goes to show there was provision to crossing the road at the spot of the accident.
As per the Ex.R1 insurance policy was valid as on the date of accident.
Hence, in the absence of breach of any policy conditions.
Therefore, the Respondent No.1 and 2 are jointly and severally liable to satisfy the award amount.
The Respondent No.2, who is liable to indemnify the Respondent No.1, has to pay the compensation amount to the Petitioner.

Accordingly, I answer Issue No.2 is "Partly in the Affirmative".
23. Issue No.3:

In view of my findings on Issues No. 1 and 2, I proceed to pass the following:
ORDER
The Claim Petition filed by the U/S 166 of M.V. Act is hereby allowed in part with costs.

SCCH 15 20 MVC No.1529/2023  The Petitioner is entitled for  Compensation of 4,67,626/- along with interest at the rate of 6% per annum from the date of the Petition till the date of deposit of Award amount.
The Respondent No.1 and 2 are jointly and severally liable to pay compensation amount to the Petitioner.
The Respondent No.2 being the insurer of the Offending vehicle, is directed to deposit the Award amount and interest within 60 days from the date of the Award.
Out of the compensation amount awarded to the Petitioner, 75% of the award amount with accrued interest shall be released to the Petitioner by way of E- payment and after proper identification.
The remaining 25% award amount shall be deposited as F.D. in the name of the Petitioner in any Nationalized or Scheduled bank for a period of three years.
The Advocate fee is fixed at 1,000/-.
SCCH 15 21 MVC No.1529/2023 Draw Award accordingly.
